extracted.intended_audience: readers, microfiction writers, and literary editors/publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Creating very short fiction pieces constrained to roughly 100 words that still convey characters, plot, and emotional impact; suitable for submission to flash fiction markets and contests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microfiction length (100 words)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page groups these pieces explicitly as 100-word stories, implying a strict or expected word-count constraint for the form and for submissions/competitions (e.g., NYC Midnight100).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of storytelling / pack story and characters
rubrics_metrics.description: "You have a talent for microfiction and for packing a lot of story and characters into a tiny amount of words."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies a key criterion for successful microfiction: efficient use of language to suggest character, plot, and emotional stakes within very limited word space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional and literary impact: engaging, resonant, memorable
rubrics_metrics.description: "Thank you very much for sending your engaging, resonant and memorable microfiction."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors look for pieces that make an emotional or aesthetic impression despite brevity—engaging voice, resonance, and memorability are valued qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit for target publication / editorial taste
rubrics_metrics.description: "The stories you have sent so far have been exactly the type of stories we look for at The Centifictionist and have been some of the fastest acceptances."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals that alignment with a publication's particular tastes and expectations is an important practical criterion for acceptance; tailoring submissions to the outlet increases chances of quick acceptance.
